purpose: Synthetic instruction-planning probes; not issuer facts, live invocations or calibrated financial-quality evaluations.

cases.request: Assess whether SYNBANK's latest growth proves a stronger underwriting moat and give a useful next check for a public retail investor.
evidence: Synthetic issuer release R1, quarter ended 2026-06-30, table 2: revenue grew 30%; interest rates rose; customer/product mix changed.
Synthetic call C1 segment 18, CFO: Our proprietary underwriting is superior. No vintage-level losses or model comparisons were disclosed.
R1 table 4 discloses aggregate delinquency and credit-loss expense. Comparative definitions are unchanged. No private customer data is available.
expected: Separate management claim and growth outcome from proof of underwriting mechanism; consider rates and mix as alternative causes.
Describe the underwriting advantage as unproven from supplied public evidence, not a failed moat.
Use the next issuer release's aggregate delinquency/credit-loss disclosures as a limited proxy; identify the limitation and consequence without invented thresholds or private cohort homework.
cases.held_out_request: Can we infer a durable credit-selection edge from this quarter? Tell me what I could actually verify using public disclosures.

cases.request: Report what management answered or left open in this earnings exchange.
evidence: Synthetic call C2 has complete relevant exchange, no omitted response turns. Segment 41, analyst: What drove margin expansion, and did retention improve?
Segment 42, CFO: Mix helped. Segment 43, CEO: Pricing also helped. Segment 44, analyst: Can you quantify those effects and answer retention?
Segment 45, CFO: Mix added two percentage points and pricing added one. Segment 46, CEO: We are not disclosing retention figures. No other retention response occurs.
expected: Recover all response/follow-up turns before classifying components.
Margin drivers and quantification were answered, including later response; retention figures were explicitly declined, leaving improvement unresolved.
Cite segment locators and report the material gap neutrally; do not infer deception or poor retention from the refusal.

cases.request: Did management avoid the analyst's question about renewal pricing?
evidence: Synthetic call C3 includes segments 1-50 only. Q&A has 80 segments; segments 51-80 were omitted by a context prefix limit.
Segment 50, analyst: Can you quantify renewal pricing and discounting? No management response is in the supplied prefix.
expected: Classify insufficient transcript evidence, not not-addressed or avoidance.
Request the complete relevant response/follow-up turns through the existing transcript route and retain the coverage limit.
Do not claim full-call review, topic disappearance or management motive.
cases.held_out_request: The available excerpt ends at the pricing question. Is that evidence of a non-answer?

cases.request: Has the CFO become more pessimistic on demand?
evidence: Synthetic prior call C4, prepared remarks segment 7, former CFO Alex: Demand remains strong.
Synthetic current call C5, Q&A segment 38, new CFO Sam answering a question about downside risks: We remain cautious about the macro environment.
No same-speaker/same-topic/context comparison is available. Both calls are text-only.
expected: Do not infer a personal CFO sentiment change across different speakers and contexts.
Identify possible management-level wording difference with personnel/question-context limits, or leave the comparison unsupported.
Do not infer vocal emotion or numeric/calibrated sentiment from text.

cases.request: Write the five-section post-earnings readout for the quarter ended 2026-03-31, including whether it beat our pre-call expectations.
evidence: Synthetic issuer release R6 dated 2026-05-01: quarter revenue 110, on the same basis as management guidance of 100-105 dated 2026-02-01 in R5 table 1.
No saved owner pre-call brief and no consensus source are available.
Context contains a current July model revision and June KPI observations, both later than the May call. The runtime has not enforced the historical cutoff.
expected: Preserve the five existing post-earnings sections and exact requested fiscal quarter.
Compare revenue with dated management guidance only; owner expectation and consensus comparisons are unavailable.
Separate subsequent model/KPI context from what was known at the call; do not present mixed context as an event-time reconstruction or invent a saved baseline.

cases.request: Management sounds confident. Should we call our portfolio thesis intact or change its break threshold?
evidence: Synthetic approved rule version T7-r2 and deterministic evaluation receipt E7: comparable admitted metric A breached its accepted break condition.
Metric B is unavailable; its binding has not been admitted. Current CEO says long-term prospects are excellent.
No owner amendment approval or revised model assumptions exist.
expected: Preserve the confirmed breach and disclose the additional unresolved input; no all-clear result from confidence or incomplete evidence.
Do not change accepted thresholds or infer an approved amendment.
Identify review/re-underwriting and the next supported public evidence; do not invent fair value or position size.

cases.request: Produce a short investment thesis and recommended position size for SYNSOFT, a company under initial evaluation.
evidence: Synthetic annual filing R8 establishes the product and revenue model. No accepted thesis, supported valuation recipe, current model assumptions or full-account portfolio snapshot is available.
Only a draft switching-cost hypothesis exists. Retention is not disclosed; risk factors name migration and competitor pricing risks.
expected: Label the hypothesis preliminary, test public support and the company-specific counter, and state coverage/valuation limits.
Give the next public proof; do not invent a quantified central bet, non-consensus risks, fair value or readiness.
Route sizing to allocation with full-book context; do not silently change evaluation level or create an accepted thesis.

cases.request: What does operating margin mean? One sentence, please.
expected: Give a concise definition; do not impose company research, moat tests, transcript collection, a model or a memo.
